Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI agent panel. On October 19, 2026 Kenneth decided: intent and plan are stored once per chat (normalized; the active chat link selects the current one), a new chat copies the active chat's intent with no plan, region annotations belong with the model version, a missing headline just omits the card line, the overrides note stays, the origin field goes, and the live eval batch is approved. A separate side chat also decided that only the in-app agent's own edits stop marking the plan stale. All of these are written into the handoff file, which is the source of truth for this task.

Task:
Implement the handoff at /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/handoff-setup-card-headline.md (read it from the main checkout; it is untracked and must stay untracked: never commit it or add it to an ignore file). Do the "Data ownership" part first: move print intent, plan and purposeSetup onto each chat, derive the current ones from the active chat, a new chat copies the active chat's intent and starts with no plan, drop the checkpoint planning copy, regions owned with the model version, schema migration. Then replace the setup card's preset-difference rows with the plan headline, make plan_set's headline concise, stop the in-app agent's own edits marking the plan stale, keep the "N objects with overrides" note, and remove the attribution layer, ranking and the model-visible origin field. Done means: every check under "Verification and completion" has been run and reported, including the approved live batch (4 journeys, DeepSeek V4 Flash, 1 run each; any rerun needs Kenneth's approval), and the final report covers everything listed in the handoff's last paragraph. Commit to your own branch only after the checks pass; don't push.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_2012258e-6e8e-4c8c-bb42-733d62a15120

Move intent/plan/purposeSetup onto each chat
Regions with model version + schema migration
Setup card headline, plan_set headline, staleness
Remove attribution layer, ranking, origin field
Run verification checks and live batch
Commit to own branch and report

# Store intent and plan on each chat, and replace setup card differences with a concise strategy headline

Replace the setup card’s preset-difference rows with the existing model-written `plan.headline`. Make the headline concise and remove every implementation path that becomes obsolete, including tracking, comparison, attribution, ranking, transport, and tests maintained only for those rows. Deliver a simpler implementation, not a new display layered over the old machinery.

The same task moves the print intent and the plan from the project onto each chat, so each is stored exactly once. The card's headline then comes from the chat it belongs to. See "Data ownership: intent and plan belong to each chat"; do that part first, because the card reads from it.

This is an implementation handoff requested by Kenneth on October 19, 2026. Production code has not been changed. Keep this temporary document untracked; do not commit it or add it to an ignore file.

## User requirements and scope

Kenneth explicitly requested both of the following:

1. Change the prompt that generates `headline` so the result is more concise.
2. Remove all code made obsolete by replacing the subtitle, including code used only to track, compare, or rank the differences shown there.
3. Store intent and plan once, on each chat, and derive the project's current intent and plan from the active chat (decided October 19; see "Data ownership").

Here, “subtitle” means the explanatory area currently showing up to two preset differences, such as `G-code thumbnails: 48x48/PNG,300x300/PNG → 48x48/PNG, 300x300/PNG`. It does not mean the purpose title or the selected-preset line. Keep the purpose title, preset identity, estimates, printer findings, and existing navigation unless an adjustment is necessary for this replacement.

The strategy headline answers how the agent proposes to print the object. `setupTitle`, stored as `setupIntent`, answers what the user wants. `conversation.title` is a separately generated chat label. Do not merge these fields or change the chat-title generator.

## Current behavior and entry points

Paths below are relative to this repository. Recheck symbols against the current checkout before editing; other work may be in progress.

| Location | Relevant behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` | `orderedPresetDeltas`, `ChangeRows`, `overrideObjectCount`, and the component’s `ordered` / `shown` / `remaining` / `note` calculations generate the difference area. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupPage.tsx` | The detailed page also consumes the deltas, `orderedPresetDeltas`, and `ChangeRows`. It separately displays object overrides. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` | `context_json` serializes differences; `remember_agent_authored`, `rebuild_agent_authored`, and `agent_authored_keys` track which current differences belong to the agent. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.hpp` | Holds the attribution methods and `m_agent_authored` / `m_agent_authored_presets` maps. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` | `preset_deltas_of` builds the differences. `setting_edits` and `record_settings_edits` also use them to detect changes for the chat history. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp` and `AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts` | Define `PresetDelta`, `PresetDeltaInfo`, and the snapshot/context payloads. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp` | Formats difference rows, but also formats edit-history values and object overrides. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp` | Defines `plan_set`, its prompt, and the required `headline` argument. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` | Accepts the model’s headline and calls `set_plan`; returns the plan in tool results. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp` | Persists the headline with the plan, tracks plan validity, and saves/restores planning snapshots. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp` | `on_edit` records changes and marks the plan `needs_reassessment` on every edit, whoever made it. This handoff changes that; see "Display and freshness". `record_chat_restore` copies a chat's saved planning snapshot back onto the project when the chat is resumed. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.cpp` / `.hpp` (conversations) | `setupIntent` is stored per chat and copied into a new chat by `create_conversation` and into the replacement chat by `delete_conversation`. `printIntent`, `plan`, `purposeSetup` and `regions` are top-level project keys. `planning_snapshot`, `save_chat_checkpoint`, `chat_checkpoint` and `restore_planning_snapshot` copy them into and out of each chat's `resumeCheckpoint`. |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (chats) | `checkpoint_active_chat` saves the leaving chat's checkpoint, including a card summary built by `context_json` that carries `setupIntent`. `handle_create_conversation`, `handle_restore_conversation` and `handle_delete_conversation` drive the transitions. Each model request reads `document.plan()` (around line 2388). |
| `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp` | The chat-resume and version-restore paths (around lines 1129–1250) call `record_chat_restore` / `record_managed_restore` and `validate_regions`. |

The plan is already sent back to the model on later turns and is available through `workspace_inspect`. At investigation time no UI component rendered its headline. Expose the existing persisted field to the card (after the move, the chat's own plan); do not create a second strategy-summary store or a separate summarization model call.

## Data ownership: intent and plan belong to each chat

Kenneth decided this on October 19, 2026. Each fact is stored once, on its owner. A chat owns its intent and its plan. The document already records which chat is active (`activeConversationId`), so the project's current intent and plan are simply the active chat's, read through that link and never stored a second time.

Today the same data lives in several places. The plan, print intent and purpose setup sit at the top of the project document, a copy goes into each chat's checkpoint when you leave it, and the copy is written back when you resume it. The per-chat setup title and the project-level purpose fields can also disagree: a second chat can be titled "Quick fit check" while the project's fields still describe a load-bearing final part. Remove the duplication rather than syncing it.

Target design:

- **What a chat holds.** Its setup title (`setupIntent`, as today), its print intent fields, its `purposeSetup` (the setup in force when the model last checked it against the purpose, which belongs with the intent), and its plan, including `validity` and `invalidatedBy`.
- **Readers.** Every reader of `plan()`, `print_intent()` and `purpose_setup()` reads the active chat's record: model requests, tool results, `workspace_inspect`, `plan_set`, `intent_update`, the setup-changed skill checks, and plan invalidation. Only the active chat's plan is ever marked stale; an inactive chat can't be edited, so nothing marks it.
- **New chat.** It starts with a copy of the active chat's intent (setup title, print intent fields and `purposeSetup`) and with no plan. A copy taken at creation is the new chat's own starting value, which it may change; it is not a duplicate that must stay in sync. The replacement chat that `delete_conversation` creates follows the same rule. The model in a new chat therefore sees no plan until it calls `plan_set`; today it inherits the previous chat's. Note this in the commit as a change to the model's input.
- **Resuming a chat.** Make it active and restore its pinned model version. Don't copy intent or plan, because they never left the chat. Its plan keeps the validity it had when you left it, which still describes that model version.
- **Chat checkpoint.** It keeps what only it can hold: the pinned model version, the boundary, the time, and the card summary for that moment (estimates, presets, findings). Drop the `planning` copy. Don't keep `setupIntent` or the headline inside the summary either: a saved card reads both from its own chat. A snapshot that records a fixed moment, such as the card for a sliced and sent build, may keep the headline it was sent with, because that is history rather than a second copy of a live record.
- **Region annotations belong with the model, not the chat.** A region record labels modifier volumes, paint or per-object overrides that live in the model itself. Today they are a top-level project key, copied into each chat checkpoint and written back on resume. Keep one copy, owned with the model version, so that restoring or resuming a model version brings back that version's regions without a checkpoint copy. Not yet verified: whether a model version's stored `semantic_state` already carries them, and how version restore treats them today (`record_managed_restore` appears to keep the current document's regions and then run `validate_regions`). Establish the mechanism, report it, and don't introduce a third copy.
- **Stale comment.** The comment above the change-log section in `ProjectStateDocument.hpp` says version restore takes "the earlier version's project-specific intent and plan". The restore path in `ProjectAutosave.cpp` appears to keep the current document instead. Verify which is true, and correct the comment to match the new ownership.

Migration (bump `ProjectStateDocument::kSchemaVersion`; .3mf and project-document backward compatibility is required):

- The active chat takes the top-level `printIntent`, `plan` and `purposeSetup`.
- Each inactive chat with a valid `resumeCheckpoint` takes that checkpoint's `planning` copy as its own intent and plan. Then drop `planning` from the checkpoint.
- An inactive chat with no checkpoint keeps its setup title and gets empty print intent fields and no plan. That is the truth for it: `chat_checkpoint` already treats a missing checkpoint as unknown historical state.
- Regions move according to the region decision above.
- Test migration from a schema-3 document with an active chat, an inactive chat with a checkpoint, and an inactive chat without one.

## Headline generation

Update the authoritative `plan_set` instructions and any necessary skill instructions. Keep detailed rationale in the existing decisions, assumptions, and risks fields rather than squeezing it into the headline.

Suggested wording to refine and evaluate:

> Write headline as a short description of the printing strategy, aiming for 8–12 words. Name the most important choices or tradeoff. Do not repeat the user’s purpose, model filename, or routine preparation steps. Put explanations in decisions, assumptions, and risks. Refresh the headline when the strategy changes.

These are illustrative targets, not live-test evidence:

- “Four walls and gyroid infill for strength”
- “Fine layers with supports away from visible surfaces”
- “Spiral vase with a continuous single wall”
- “Coarse layers and low infill for a quick fit check”

Avoid headlines such as “Prepare the loaded model for printing” or “Repair the mesh before slicing.” Do not invent settings just to make a headline sound specific. Adapt the length target to the user’s language; avoid adding brittle validation or cutting sentences mid-word merely to enforce the English word target.

Update prompt fixtures and generated tool definitions through the documented workflow. Evaluate actual model output, not just whether the new sentence exists in a fixture.

## Display and freshness

Use `plan.headline` for the replacement text. With no headline, omit the strategy line: no placeholder, no fallback to preset differences, no copy of the intent. Kenneth accepted on October 19 that some journeys never call `plan_set` (the October 12 `B-hook` journey didn't, and the model is only told to call it before several changes), so those cards are simply shorter. Don't change when the model calls `plan_set` in this task; the live evaluation reports how often the headline is missing. Missing headlines in older saved projects must be supported.

### Decision: the agent's own edits no longer make its plan stale

Kenneth decided this on October 19, 2026.

Today every edit marks the plan `needs_reassessment`, including the in-app agent's own edits: `ProjectPersistence::on_edit` never looks at `edit.actor`. The model is told to call `plan_set` before applying several changes, so in the normal journey the plan is marked stale by the very edits that carry it out. The recorded prompt-eval requests show it happening. After `plan_set`, the agent's own `printer_setup` and `settings_apply_patch` calls mark the plan stale, with `invalidatedBy` set to "Sparse infill pattern" or "Bambu PETG HF @BBL X1C". Of the 381 `planValidity` values in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json`, 240 are `needs_reassessment`.

This applies the principle Kenneth set on October 19 for the project-setup-changed skill, which no longer fires on the model's own `printer_setup`: the model does not need a reminder about a change it just decided to make. Plan invalidation changes to match:

- An edit whose actor is `EditActor::Agent` no longer marks the plan. That actor means the in-app agent; `ToolExecutionCoordinator` sets it for every call whose source is not MCP.
- A person's edit (`EditActor::Person`) still marks the plan. That includes hand edits in OrcaSlicer and the Undo and Redo the person triggers; confirm that the card's Undo button records `Person`.
- An external MCP client's edit (`EditActor::ExternalTool`) still marks the plan. Another agent changing the project is not the in-app agent carrying out its own plan.
- Restoring an earlier model version (`ProjectPersistence::record_managed_restore`) still marks the plan. Resuming a chat makes its own plan current again with the validity it had; see "Data ownership".

Make the change in `on_edit` only. Leave `mark_plan_needs_reassessment` and the restore path as they are, and keep recording every edit in the change log. What the model reads changes too: plan validity in tool results and in each turn's workspace block now stays `current` after the agent's own edits. Re-record the prompt-eval requests and say in the commit that this is an intentional change to the model's input. Update native tests that expect an agent edit to invalidate the plan. Add tests showing that an in-app agent edit leaves the plan current, while a person's edit, an external MCP edit and a version restore each mark it.

One limit is accepted. If the agent changes strategy through its own edits without calling `plan_set` again, as in the October 12 vase journey, the plan stays `current` with the old headline. The prompt's instruction to refresh the headline when the strategy changes is what covers this case. The live evaluation must report how often it happens.

### Card rule: the headline follows the card's existing states

The card already defines when it can be trusted. That logic was built in 814c4e86b3 (September 8) and 4f05de4715 (October 6) and lives in `setupPresentation` in `SetupCard.tsx`. Don't add a second freshness rule for the headline, and don't read `plan.validity` on the card. When a headline exists, show it in every state, and let the existing state label and notices tell the person how far to trust the card:

- **Agent working, Updated, Confirmed, Current, Not sliced:** show the headline normally.
- **Edited by you:** show the headline. The existing notice already names the settings the person changed outside the agent and says they are kept. It comes from the change log (`handEdits`), not from preset differences, so removing the difference rows does not affect it.
- **Out of date** (the slice estimate no longer matches the project): show the headline. The card already drops its accent, reads "Earlier setup", and offers "Refresh setup & recompute".
- **Saved cards in earlier chats:** show that chat's own plan headline, under that card's saved state ("Saved", "Sliced & sent" or "Out of date"). Never show the active chat's plan there. A sliced-and-sent snapshot shows the headline it was sent with.
- **Preset fallback** (no agent configured, or no recorded purpose and no applied setup): no headline line.

A stored headline describes the agent's intended strategy. It doesn't prove that the settings were applied or that a slice passed; the card's estimate section and states cover those facts. Check that the normal journey (plan, then apply, then slice) ends with a current headline under a Current or Updated card. Also check that a hand edit afterwards shows the headline under "Edited by you", while the model sees the plan as `needs_reassessment`.

Push updated context when `plan_set` succeeds; the current special refresh path handles settings patches and `intent_update`, so merely adding a context field may leave the card stale. Check all live, saved-chat, restored-chat, and sent-snapshot paths. A historical card must show its own chat's headline and its saved state, not the active chat's plan.

## Required removal and dependency audit

Start with a consumer inventory. For each helper, field, cache, observer, and test involved in the old subtitle, classify it as removable or shared, and name the remaining consumer if retained. Follow dependencies beyond the React component.

Remove the card’s difference selection, ranking, “N more changes” count, row rendering, and “No changes from presets” behavior. Keep the “N objects with overrides” note and `overrideObjectCount` (Kenneth, October 19): it isn't a preset difference, it tells the person some objects print with their own settings, and the headline won't say that. It currently shares a line with the “more changes” count; it stands alone after the change. Remove obsolete styles, fixtures, visual cases, and assertions. Two components are named `ChangeRows`. The one exported from `SetupCard.tsx` renders preset differences for the card and the setup page. The one in `components/ChangeRows.tsx` renders the chat's change log under each agent turn (`MessageList.tsx`) and stays. Today the card's Updated state doesn't repeat the agent's changed settings because they lead the difference rows; the comment in `SetupCard` says so. Once the rows are gone, the change-log rows in the thread are the only place those settings appear. Update that comment rather than adding a list back. Do not retain dead branches, hidden fallback rows, feature flags, unused optional payloads, or compatibility shims without a real compatibility requirement.

Remove the dedicated authorship layer if no remaining feature needs it. This includes parsing successful patch results to remember exact values, replaying old tool activities to rebuild those values, binding them to preset names, clearing them when presets switch, checking current values against them, the two maps, and all call sites and refreshes whose only purpose was attribution. Preserve tool-activity persistence itself.

The detailed setup page currently reuses agent-first and recency ranking. Recommended scope: preserve its factual preset differences, but use stable preset/page/group ordering instead of that ranking. This allows removing subtitle-driven attribution and time-batch ranking completely without dropping the detailed inspection feature. Move any genuinely shared row rendering out of the card if appropriate. Remove the `origin` field and its serialization (decided October 19). It has one consumer beyond the card: the model. `context_json` also builds the workspace block returned with every in-app tool result (`AgentHost::continue_after_tool`), so `origin` appears 817 times in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json`. No prompt or skill mentions it. Remove it there too, re-record the prompt-eval requests in the same pass as the plan-validity change, and say in the commit that both are intentional changes to the model's input.

Remove any other now-unused display metadata and snapshot work. However, do not claim that all `PresetDelta` computation or all value formatting is obsolete merely because the card no longer renders differences. The detailed page still needs factual differences under the recommended scope.

The edit-history implementation also compares previous and current preset readings. It distinguishes restoring a preset value from saving that value into the preset, and detects hand edits and preset changes. Those edits feed the chat timeline, the card’s update/manual-edit states, and plan reassessment. Preserve these behaviors. If simplifying this shared code, separate raw change detection from display preparation and demonstrate equivalent behavior; do not delete it wholesale or rewrite it solely for line-count reduction.

Likewise preserve settings-tool preview/apply comparisons, stale-revision checks, project dirty state, Undo/Redo, autosave, and version restore. Those are independent of the subtitle. Removing an obsolete display does not authorize changing slicer behavior. The thumbnail comparison issue that motivated this discussion need not be patched upstream to replace the card.

## Evidence from previous live tests

The separate investigation chat is `01a155fc-1cb1-78f3-a45a-2b7e653769ab`. It found these actual model outputs:

- October 19, DeepSeek V4 Flash: “PETG print on X1 Carbon — 4 walls, 25% gyroid infill.” The one-step test captured the proposed `plan_set` call but stopped before executing it. Source: `.claude/worktrees/competent-liskov-live2.out`, around line 307.
- October 12, cosmetic figurine: “Prepare the X1 Carbon PLA job and fix the broken mesh before slicing.” The text was not refreshed after the cosmetic requirement became known. Source: `.claude/worktrees/model-nature-probe/probe/results/2026-10-12-batch/A-rhino/turn-2.json`.
- October 12, vase: “Prepare Spiral_Vase1_SOLID.STL for PLA printing on Bambu Lab X1 Carbon.” It remained generic when spiral vase mode was subsequently recommended. Source: the same batch’s `A-vase/turn-2.json`.
- The same batch’s `B-hook` journey produced no `plan_set` call.

The older journeys predate the current prompt; their logs do not establish final plan-validity flags. Repeated headlines embedded in scripted test history are not evidence of live generation. Entire session search reported no matching repository mirror; use the saved evaluation evidence if that limitation persists.

## Verification and completion

Read `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, the design-system instructions, and the relevant test READMEs before implementation. Check whether an isolated development instance is already running. Use a dedicated data directory and never automate another JusPrin instance. Keep changes in fork-owned code where possible; follow fork stewardship for any upstream-owned edits. Do not commit submodules or unrelated work.

Cover the following with appropriate component, native bridge/state, and real-app checks:

1. A concise headline reaches the card immediately after `plan_set`; purpose and chat titles are unaffected.
2. The card no longer shows preset differences, formatting-only thumbnail noise, difference counts, or an old difference fallback.
3. Empty headlines, old saved summaries, long/localized headlines, narrow panels, and no-agent mode remain readable and functional.
4. Plan validity follows the October 19 decision: the in-app agent's own settings and preset edits leave the plan `current`; a person's edits, Undo and Redo, external MCP edits and version restores mark it `needs_reassessment`. On the card, the headline appears in each of the card's existing states as listed under "Card rule", including after successful and failed slices, preset switches and a headline refresh.
5. Historical chats, restart, restore, and sent snapshots preserve their own strategy text without leaking today’s plan.
6. The detailed setup page, edit-history entries, restore controls, estimates, and plan invalidation still work after cleanup. Include saving an edited preset versus resetting its value.
7. A final symbol/consumer search finds no obsolete attribution maps, reconstruction methods, ranking logic, payload fields, or tests left behind. Explain each retained shared dependency.
8. Intent and plan are stored once per chat. A new chat starts with the active chat's intent and no plan, and the model sees no plan there. Switching, resuming and deleting chats show each chat's own intent and plan. No top-level `printIntent`/`plan`/`purposeSetup` and no checkpoint `planning` copy remain.
9. Migration from a schema-3 project covers an active chat, an inactive chat with a checkpoint, and one without. Regions survive chat resume and version restore through the one mechanism chosen.
10. The “N objects with overrides” note still appears when objects have overrides.

Run the relevant existing AgentUI and native suites and an isolated shell end-to-end journey. Update the existing setup-differences capture workflow where its card expectations are superseded, while preserving checks for details that remain. Use `tests/project_prompt/README.md` for a small live evaluation. Kenneth approved this batch on October 19: four journeys (strength, appearance/supports, a quick prototype, and a changed strategy), one model (DeepSeek V4 Flash, as in the October 19 runs), one run each. Any rerun or extra journey needs his approval first. Report exact headlines, how many journeys produced no headline, and stale cases where the strategy changed without a new `plan_set`; do not treat the October 19 unexecuted call as a completed journey. Follow credential workflows for any live model calls.

The final implementation report should state the new intent, plan and region ownership and the migration, what the card now shows, the concise prompt wording, the plan-validity change and how the headline appears in each card state, the removed tracking/comparison/ranking paths, the shared paths deliberately retained, and the checks actually run. Highlight any untested behavior. The task is not complete if the old subtitle machinery remains active behind the new text.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

On 2026-10-19 the shell harness's `--project-prompt-requests` mode was run
twice on the same build configuration, once at jusprin-newui 8913319cac and
once with the OpenAIResponsesAgent split into ProviderAgent + ResponsesCodec
(branch claude/provider-agent-extract). A structural JSON diff of the 24
cases showed 59 differing leaves, every one in four patterns:

- ISO timestamps (`updatedAt`, activity times): `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T..Z`
- view_render pictures: the base64 after `data:image/png;base64,` and the
  `"bytes":N` count beside it (the GL render is not pixel-stable run to run)
- temp paths under `/var/folders/...`
- nothing else: after replacing those, 0 differences
- also timing, seen in a later pair of runs of one binary: a print issue's
  `"evidence":{"generation":N}` off by one (issue-explain, issue-fix), and
  the after-slice case's slice_report answer taken before the slice ended
  (`"valid":false` plus a `sharedWorkspace` key instead of findings). The
  same binary differs in exactly those four leaves between two runs, so
  when they appear, record once more before suspecting the code

Each full recording takes about 3 minutes and writes ~4.6 MB.

**Why:** "byte-identical before and after" is the brief for a wire-neutral
refactor, and the raw files never are; knowing the noise set up front turns
a 59-line diff into a 0-line proof instead of an hour of reading.

**How to apply:** record before and after into the scratchpad, walk both
JSON trees leaf by leaf, normalise the four patterns on string leaves, and
expect zero. Any remaining leaf is a real change. The committed
tests/project_prompt/requests.json is older than the slice-failed skill
merge (its after-slice slice_report answer has an older shape), so diff
against a fresh baseline run, not the committed file. Related:
[[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[harness-stalls-on-version-dialog]].

name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. A point's `once` (in `requests.json`) counts
  the last items of its request that the app sends on that request alone,
  a skill's text and, for the file-loaded skill, its picture; the runner
  drops them before it answers
  a read, as the app does.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the
  recorded requests: the app adds one to the request where its event first
  reaches the model, as that request's last item. The recorder checks that a
  point the script marks `"skill": "<name>"` ends with that skill (after the
  plate's picture for `file-loaded`), that no other point
  carries a skill or a picture, so an import's point carries the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
  first answered read) has none.
  A skill edit therefore needs a new recording, unlike a prompt edit.

What is written by hand is only what a model or a person would have said: the
person's words, the scripted calls, and two assistant replies (the summary
after the prepare turn and the first message about an opened file). The
scripted calls carry the replay form the app uses (`call_id`, `name`,
`arguments`); a live model's own item id, status and reasoning items within a
turn are not reproducible. Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current:
record it again when a tool's results, the fixture or the request shape
change. It was recorded with the change that moved the workspace snapshot

temporary path. Recorded again when the app began asking for several calls
per response (`parallel_tool_calls: true`): only that flag, ids, timestamps

The app streams its requests and this script does not.

What the suite is for (Kenneth, 2026-10-19): showing that a change has not
made the prompt substantially worse. At three runs a case it detects large
regressions only, not small effects. Day-to-day host noise is small next to
what it looks for: on the printer suite the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74
of 84 on three runs.

1. After a prompt or skill change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout,
   same model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
   current baseline table below. There is no before run.

content.text: That design doc still describes intent and plan as project-level fields, so I'm correcting it.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md'
s=open(p).read()
old="""An imported project may contain the older `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json` and its recovery mirror. Those are read only to migrate them. Three things remain fields of that document:
  - the print intent, `printIntent`. A write inserts or updates one field by name, and each field carries its provenance;
  - the plan, `plan`. A write replaces the whole plan;
  - the region annotations, `regions`. A write replaces the whole list, and each record is stamped with a seq when it changes.
"""
new="""An imported project may contain the older `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json` and its recovery mirror. Those are read only to migrate them. In that document:
  - each chat owns its print intent, `printIntent`, and its plan, `plan` (with the setup title and the purpose setup beside them). The project's current intent and plan are the active chat's, read through `activeConversationId` and stored nowhere else; a new chat starts with a copy of the active chat's intent and no plan. An intent write inserts or updates one field by name, and each field carries its provenance; a plan write replaces the whole plan;
  - the region annotations, `regions`, describe the model in the workspace. A write replaces the whole list, and each record is stamped with a seq when it changes. Every saved model version records the list it was saved with, and restoring or resuming that version puts its list back.
"""
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n -i "region\|chat" agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md | head -30

version so it can be reopened; later document edits do not add versions. A
first Agent model operation pins that baseline as its before-version.
Conversation, intent, plan, region descriptions,
audit, and completed print records remain in the current document. Restoring a
model does not undo physical prints or change global printer facts. Agent
mutations save and pin their actual
before-state, then link an after-version and outcome in an operation record.

## Storage and recovery contract

The restoration rules above describe ordinary Version history. **Restore and
resume** is a separate chat transition. Each active chat keeps a checkpoint
with a model-version reference, matching print intent, plan and region
annotations, and a structured setup summary. Browsing an older chat does not
change the working project. Resuming it saves and pins the outgoing state,
restores the model and matching planning fields, and activates that chat only
after the new document is durable. Other conversations, audit and print
records, and global printer facts remain. This does not add a full project-
document copy to model versions or make document edits create model versions.
Ordinary Version history remains model-only and does not activate an older
chat. An interrupted chat transition leaves a durable pending marker and
blocks that managed project for explicit recovery on restart.

Each model version has Orca backup-format metadata and a manifest of object
resources. It has no copy of the project document. Unchanged object resources are referenced rather
than serialized again. Changed objects are serialized with Orca's split-model
writer into immutable ZIP resources. A renamed object can reuse its resource;
materialization relabels its entry for Orca's native restore loader. Metadata
and each resource are checked for required entries and geometry. The live
Orca backup directory and an imported source file are never version-store
dependencies.

All project records advance one `current-state.json` document without creating
a model version. The document is atomically replaced after 1.5 seconds without
a change, or within 15 seconds during a continuous stream. Agent and project
boundaries wait for the write. Attachments are written once before their
document references become durable; operation records linking before/after
versions are committed once at the operation boundary. A model checkpoint
ensures the current document is durable before it publishes a new `HEAD`.

## Save classification

The autosave controller observes two independent kinds of change. Native
geometry, transforms, paint, plates, and effective project settings can change
what an earlier printable project reconstructs and therefore create a model
version. Document changes, including streamed Agent messages, drafts, intent,
plans, region descriptions, audit records, and print facts, update only the
current document. `docRevision` is a signal to coalesce that write; neither
it nor document contents participate in model-version equality. A workspace
event can prompt a model check, but cannot make unchanged checkpoint content
into a new version.

A single writer owns each project through an OS file lock. It writes and
flushes the current document and changed resources before publishing a version directory,
then atomically replaces `HEAD` with the ordered committed-version index.

function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

and the next save retries it. Project replacement is blocked until the live
state is saved. Explicit export validates a temporary 3MF before replacing
its destination.

Older projects may still contain `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json` and a
recovery mirror. On first adoption, JusPrin reads that state and copies its
attachments to the managed store; it does not delete the old source. Once a
managed version exists, local state is authoritative. Reopening a copied
external 3MF with an already managed identity forks a new project identity.
When a file opened as a project matches a saved project, JusPrin asks whether
to create another project or open the existing one directly. A project
remembers the file it was opened from (`openedFrom`) and that file's MD5 then
(`openedDigest`) in each version manifest: a .3mf from its project path, a model
file the agent's `project_open` opened as a new project from the path it gave.
Every way a person opens a .3mf asks, because the check sits in
`Plater::load_project` (File > Open Project, recent files, Finder, drops); the
agent's `project_open` returns the question as `opened_before` and takes the
answer as `openedBefore`. A file whose MD5 differs is a likely new export, so
the question says so and defaults to a new project; otherwise it defaults to
the saved one. Versions saved before 2026-10-14 have no digest and are asked
about as unchanged. Importing a file into a project never asks. If several
projects match, it continues the current one when it came from that file;
otherwise it opens the most recently updated match.

remain readable; the first new document write upgrades them to the independent

content.text:
I've committed f964221268 on `claude/setup-card-headline` (cut from `jusprin-newui` 8913319cac, not pushed). The setup card now shows the plan's headline instead of preset differences, each chat stores its own intent and plan, and the schema is back to version 1 with no migration. All native, page and shell-harness checks pass, and the approved live batch ran: 12 of 12 journeys produced a headline.

**Where things are stored now**
- **Intent and plan:** each chat stores its own print intent, purpose setup and plan. The project's current ones are the active chat's, stored nowhere else.
- **New chats:** a new chat (or the replacement made when the active chat is deleted) copies the active chat's intent and starts with no plan. So the model in a new chat sees no plan until it calls `plan_set`.
- **Resuming a chat:** it becomes active and its model version comes back. Nothing is copied, because the chat's plan never left it.
- **Chat checkpoints:** they no longer hold a planning copy, setup title or headline. A saved chat's card reads those from its own chat.
- **Regions:** saved model versions turned out to hold no project-document data at all. Restore always kept the current document, so the old header comment claiming otherwise was wrong, and I've corrected it. Each version now records its own region list; restoring or resuming it puts that list back, and a region change counts as a new version.
- **Schema reset to 1:** done as Kenneth asked. A document of any other version loads as a fresh one, so **project files saved during development lose their chats**. I also removed the old-record reads in the version store and autosave.

**Kept on purpose:**
- **Auxiliary `state.json` import:** the persistence layer still reads a `state.json` carried inside an imported `.3mf`, plus the older non-managed storage mode. That's an import path that most tests also use, not a schema migration; removing it would be a larger refactor if he wants it gone.
- **Home preview fallback:** Home still uses the original file's thumbnail when a project's latest version hasn't been rendered. That's a normal path, not legacy.

**The card**
- The headline appears under the presets line in every state: Agent working, Updated, Confirmed, Current, Not sliced, Edited by you, Out of date, Saved, and Sliced & sent. A saved card shows its own chat's headline.
- With no plan, or on the preset fallback card, there's no line and no stand-in.
- "N objects with overrides" stands alone on its own line.
- `plan_set` pushes the headline to the card as soon as it succeeds.
- The detailed setup page keeps every difference, now in OrcaSlicer's own order.
- **Removed:** the card's difference rows, the ranking, the "more changes" count, "No changes from presets", the whole record of which settings the agent wrote, and the `origin` field.

**Plan validity:** the in-app agent's own edits no longer mark its plan as needing reassessment. A person's edits, Undo and Redo, external MCP clients' edits and version restores still do. A test of this fails when the old behaviour is put back.

**Prompt wording:** `plan_set` now asks for the strategy in about 8 to 12 words in English, without repeating the purpose, file name, printer or routine preparation steps, and for a refresh when the strategy changes.

**Checks run, all passing:**
- 338 agent-bridge test cases, plus the workspace contract, setting display and JusPrin suites.
- 444 page tests.
- Shell harness: the default run (561 checks), chat restoration, and the setup-differences capture, extended for the headline and a hand edit.
- The real-adapter harness, including four new region checks.
- `project_tools.json` was regenerated with one line changed. `requests.json` was re-recorded: `origin` dropped from 818 occurrences to 0, and `needs_reassessment` from 240 to 0. Nothing else changed beyond known timing noise.

**Batch B (DeepSeek V4 Flash, pinned hosts):**
- **Cost:** the pilot used 277k input tokens, so I ran the rest. The batch total was 235 requests, 4,501,399 input tokens (3,681,024 cached) and 90,984 output.
- **Pictures stripped:** the pinned hosts reject image input, so the journey runner removed the plate pictures from every request and the model never saw them.
- **Answering:** I answered the model's questions with "Yes, go ahead" plus the plate when asked.

| Run | Final headline | Words | Card at end |
|---|---|---|---|
| strength-1 | PETG wall hook with strong walls, high infill, and proper bed choice | 12 | Updated, shown |
| strength-2 | PETG Strength preset with 4+ walls on Textured PEI Plate | 10 | Current, shown |
| strength-3 | PETG wall hook, mounting face down, Strength profile for 5 kg load | 12 | Current, shown |
| appearance-1 | Rhino figurine — fine detail, organic supports, hidden contact points | 10 | Current, shown |
| appearance-2 | Fine-layer rhino upright, no supports, seam hidden at back | 9 | Updated, shown |
| appearance-3 | Rhino figurine standing upright with fine detail, minimal visible supports | 10 | Updated, shown |
| quick-1 | Fast draft fit check: 0.28mm layer height, minimal infill, 2 walls | 11 | Updated, shown |
| quick-2 | Extra Draft preset, 2 walls, minimal infill, for fastest fit check | 11 | Updated, shown |
| quick-3 | Draft-quality fit check, thickest layers for speed | 7 | Current, shown |
| changed-1 | Spiral vase mode, PLA, smooth single-wall dried-flower display → Multi-wall watertight vase, PLA, 5 walls, 6 bottom layers | 8 → 9 | Updated, shown |
| changed-2 | Spiral vase mode: single-wall continuous print with open top for flowers → Multi-wall print, thick solid base, and infill for a watertight, carryable vase | 11 → 12 | Current, shown |
| changed-3 | Spiral vase mode for a lightweight, single-wall dried-flower vase → Multi-wall vase with infill for watertight strength, PLA on X1 Carbon | 9 → 11 | Current, shown |

All 12 called `plan_set`. In all three changed-strategy runs the headline was rewritten after the second message; none was left stale. "Updated" just means the agent's last change was under a minute old when the card was captured.

**What looks wrong in the batch:**
- **Headlines still repeat things the prompt excludes.** Five name the object ("PETG wall hook", "Rhino figurine"). strength-3 repeats the purpose ("for 5 kg load"), changed-3 names the printer, and strength-1 ends with routine preparation ("proper bed choice").
- **The setup title went stale after the change of goal.** In changed-2 and changed-3 the title still read "spiral vase" for dried flowers while the headline said multi-wall watertight. The title is the purpose record and the model didn't update it.
- **changed-3's headline got ahead of its settings.** The headline changed before any setting did, so the card showed the new strategy over the old spiral-vase estimates. The handoff accepts that a headline states intent, not applied settings.
- **changed-2 was expensive.** It made 39 requests (948k input tokens) and stopped to ask a design question: the vase file is a solid body, so holding water needs a cut or a different file. Both changed-strategy runs 2 and 3 stopped on that question, and I ended them there.

**Not tested end to end:** that the card's Undo button records the person. The code shows it does, and Undo and Redo marking the plan stale is covered with the fake workspace, but not through the real button.

The handoff stays untracked. The journey runner is kept out of the commit and saved, with the batch transcripts, in the shared notes folder as `plan-journey-harness-mode.patch` and `plan-journey-batch-b/`.

Kenneth wants intent_update and plan_set merged into one tool, built on claude/setup-card-headline (on top of f964221268). His words: "Send the merged-tool design to the implementation session to build on claude/setup-card-headline. No live runs until I approve a batch."

Why: in batch B's changed-strategy runs 2 and 3, the model rewrote the plan headline with plan_set but never called intent_update. The card's title still said spiral vase above a multi-wall watertight headline. The two records are already handled as one: same handler block in ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp, both in-app only, both stored on the chat, the same context push (AgentHost.cpp around line 721). Together they make up the card.

The design Kenneth agreed to:
- One tool that records the chat's purpose and plan. Suggested name `setup_record`; keep neither old name.
- `setupTitle` is required on every call, so the plan can't change without the title being restated.
- Intent `fields` stay optional, with today's semantics (assumed flag, question, provenance).
- The plan (headline, decisions, assumptions, risks) is optional. When present it replaces the whole plan, as plan_set does now. When absent, the current plan is kept. That covers recording a purpose before a strategy exists: a title-only call, then the setup check, then a later call with the plan.
- Keep the concise-headline wording you added. Have the description state the split: the title is what the user wants, the headline is how the agent will print it.

What has to move with it:
- purpose_changed (AgentHost.cpp around line 494) and the setup-changed skill trigger it feeds: key on the merged tool, and fire only when the title or fields actually changed (first or changed purpose), never on a call that only changes the plan.
- Anything else keyed on ToolHandler::IntentUpdate / PlanSet or on either tool name: mark_setup_checked paths, the activity-title builder in ToolRegistry.cpp around line 1794, protocol/page code, history replay.

content.text:
`intent_update` and `plan_set` are now one tool, `setup_record`, committed as 28d6d67fdc on `claude/setup-card-headline`, on top of f964221268 and not pushed. All native, page and shell-harness tests pass. I made no live-model calls.

**How the tool works**
- **`setupTitle`** is required on every call. It's what the person wants, and it's the card's title. A title the chat refuses (more than one line or over 120 characters) records nothing, plan included.
- **`fields`** are optional and behave as before.
- **`plan`** is optional (headline, decisions, assumptions, risks). When given it replaces the whole plan; when left out the plan is kept. So a purpose can be recorded before there's a strategy, and the plan added in a later call.
- **The result** always includes the plan as it now stands.
- **The description** keeps the concise-headline wording and says the title is what the person wants and the headline is how the agent will print it.
- **The card** gets title and headline in one push per call.

**Decision for Kenneth:** the setup-check skill fires only when a call records a first purpose or changes its fields, as before. A call that only rewords the title doesn't fire it, and neither does a plan-only call. The request said "when the title or fields actually changed".
